correctness.rationale: For C4-free G, any set of four vertices with all triples connected would have minimum induced degree two and hence contain a four-cycle. The Alexander dual therefore has a complete 1-skeleton, connected triples as its only 2-faces and no higher faces. Every induced P3 is collapsed along its unique nonadjacent endpoint pair; every remaining graph triangle has a graph edge belonging to no other triangle, so it too collapses. The connected residual graph has cycle rank C(n-1,2)-sum_v C(deg(v),2)+2t. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality yields top homology only; the complete (n-5)-skeleton plus Hurewicz and Whitehead gives a wedge of (n-4)-spheres. This exact argument establishes the all-graph quantifier, supplemented by directly replayed collapse and mod-two checks on triangle-containing examples.

value.rationale: The result gives a full integral and homotopy classification for an infinite natural graph class permitting triangles and arbitrary nonchordal structure, rather than an Euler number or finite census. The nonchordal truncated tetrahedral graph has 27 top-dimensional spheres in dimension eight. The new triangle correction and uniform two-stage collapse identify a structural boundary precisely at the first possible four-cycle. The conclusion is not confined to an arbitrary small slice.
